ASTRA — Astronaut Health Intelligence & Monitoring Platform
ASTRA is an AI-powered platform that helps astronauts and mission teams monitor health, detect unusual patterns, assess potential risks, and make informed decisions during space missions.

CORE FEATURES:
- Mission dashboards with astronaut status, alerts, and health trends.
- Astronaut profiles with individual measurements and health history.
- Analytics for heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure, temperature, respiration, sleep, and activity.
- PDF, CSV, and JSON data upload and validation.
- Anomaly detection using Isolation Forest, Z-scores, and NASA-based thresholds.
- Gemini AI assistant for health insights and anomaly explanations.
- Alert management with severity levels and acknowledgment.
- Downloadable PDF health reports.

SCIENTIFIC FOUNDATION:
NASA research on microgravity, cardiovascular changes, sleep, circadian rhythms, radiation, and astronaut health.

DEMO MODE:
Three fictional astronaut profiles, simulated telemetry, historical data, intentional anomalies, and interactive controls.

TECH STACK:
Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Lucide, Motion.
Backend: Node.js, Express, TypeScript.
Data: csv-parse, pdf-parse, JSON storage.
ML: Custom Isolation Forest, Rolling Z-score.
AI: Google GenAI SDK, Gemini API, NASA references.
Reports: jsPDF.

VISION:
Turning astronaut health data into actionable intelligence for safer space exploration.
details:
ASTRA — Astronaut Health Intelligence & Monitoring Platform

ASTRA is an AI-powered astronaut health-monitoring platform designed to help astronauts and mission teams monitor physiological indicators, identify unusual health patterns, understand potential risks, and make informed decisions during space missions.

How it works:
ASTRA brings astronaut health information together in a centralized dashboard. It processes uploaded PDF, CSV, and JSON files, extracts relevant health records, and presents the information through interactive charts and analytics. Its anomaly detection engine combines a custom Isolation Forest implementation, Rolling Z-score analysis, and NASA-based reference thresholds to identify unusual patterns. A Gemini-powered AI assistant helps interpret these findings, explain potential concerns, and provide insights grounded in NASA research. The platform also supports alerts, historical trend analysis, and downloadable PDF reports.

Benefits and intended impact:
ASTRA aims to make astronaut health information easier to monitor, interpret, and act upon. By highlighting unusual physiological patterns and presenting explainable insights, it can support more informed health-monitoring decisions, reduce the effort required to analyse complex records, and contribute to safer human space exploration. It is designed as a decision-support platform, not a medical diagnostic system.

Technology used:
The frontend uses React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Lucide React, and Motion. The backend is built with Node.js, Express, and TypeScript. Data processing uses csv-parse and pdf-parse, with JSON-based persistence. Machine learning is implemented through a custom TypeScript Isolation Forest and Rolling Z-score engine. Google GenAI SDK and Gemini power the AI assistant, while jsPDF generates reports.

Creativity and innovation:
ASTRA combines machine learning, AI-assisted interpretation, interactive health analytics, and scientific research into one integrated astronaut-monitoring platform. Its demonstration mode includes three fictional astronaut profiles, simulated telemetry, historical records, and intentionally introduced anomalies, allowing users to explore how the system responds to changing health patterns.

Factors considered:
We prioritised scientific credibility, data accuracy, explainability, usability, and reliability. NASA research and reference standards inform the monitoring logic. We also distinguish simulated data from actual records, avoid presenting statistical anomalies as confirmed medical conditions, and provide fallback functionality when the AI service is unavailable.
